findings.observation: Members routing <40% of their surveyed yield to the FPO defect next cycle 59% of the time overall — 80% in normal-rainfall seasons, only 14% after rainfall deficits.
findings.insight: Yield retention is the single strongest leading indicator, but rainfall context changes its meaning entirely — the same retention collapse is bad faith in a normal year and bad luck in a deficit one.
findings.hypothesis: Blending district rainfall deviation into the churn model separates drought-stressed members from genuine side-sellers.
findings.recommendation: Keep retention <40% as the operational trigger, but require the rainfall-context check before any loyalty action; route deficit-district cases to emergency liquidity instead.

findings.observation: Random Forest reaches AUC 0.93 / AP 0.66 out-of-time, and the top-50 monthly dispatch list is 68% precise.
findings.insight: Behavioural signals (retention trend, recency, monetary decay) predict cooperative defection well enough to run a capacity-constrained visit programme.
findings.hypothesis: Precision-first threshold tuning beats default 0.5 cut-offs when field officers can visit only 50 farms/month.
findings.recommendation: Operate at τ=0.82; review the flagged list at each monthly extension meeting; re-fit every season.

findings.observation: Removing the rainfall features costs 0.018 AUC and adds 12 false alarms per test window, concentrated on drought-hit members.
findings.insight: Without agro-climatic context the model would send officers to lecture rain-failure victims on loyalty — reputational and ethical damage.
findings.hypothesis: The drought-stress overlay is the guardrail that keeps the tool on the right side of the association-vs-causation line.
findings.recommendation: Never deploy AgriPulse without live rainfall feeds (IMD grids); audit the drought/commercial split of every dispatch list.

findings.observation: Members whose last input purchase at the FPO depot is >180 days old show 2.1× the baseline next-cycle churn.
findings.insight: Micro-transactions (fertilizer, seed, repayments) carry a continuous engagement signal that bridges the multi-month silence of crop cycles — exactly the sparsity mitigation the proposal planned.
findings.hypothesis: Input-depot activity is an early-warning channel available weeks before harvest deliveries confirm a defection.
findings.recommendation: Wire depot purchase logs into the monthly refresh; trigger a courtesy call when a delivering member stops buying inputs.

findings.observation: Precision varies only mildly across landholding classes (marginal/small/medium: 0.74–1.00) and drought-exposed members are flagged at similar rates.
findings.insight: The score does not systematically scapegoat smallholders or drought districts — the two groups most vulnerable to unfair flagging.
findings.hypothesis: Group-aware fairness auditing each cycle keeps deployment drift visible.
findings.recommendation: Keep the landholding/drought parity table in the monthly pack; escalate any subgroup precision gap >10 points to the FPO board.
